summary: Postinstall downloads and executes opaque binary from mismatched publisher; README impersonates unrelated project
details: The @apexfdn/apex package ships no source code (no src/ or bin/ directory despite package.json declaring main as./src/index.ts). Its postinstall script (install.js) downloads a platform-specific binary from https://github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot/releases/download/v1.0.1/<assetName>, writes it to disk, chmods it 0o755, and the `apex` bin wrapper executes it with the user's full inherited environment. No hash or signature is verified. The package's README is verbatim documentation for an unrelated legitimate project (@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent by can1357), and package.json advertises homepage omp.sh and repository can1357/oh-my-pi — none of which relate to the actual download source Apex-Foundation/copilot. This publisher mismatch plus impersonation of an established project's documentation is a cover-story pattern: the shipped README lends credibility to a package whose entire runtime is an unverified binary fetched from a different, unrelated GitHub org on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
